zh: 在马新贻的新命传至浙江的同时；江西来了一个重要而有趣的消息，『幼逆』洪福真终于落网了。收束平洪杨的军务，却还有相当艰巨的戡乱大任，需要部署。恭王、文祥的计议，犹有三处叛乱要平服，才能臻于太平盛世。这三处叛乱是∶第一、南窜的洪杨余孽；第二是扰乱中原的捻匪；第三是荼毒生灵、为患西陲的回乱。幸好人才旺盛，冠绝前朝；恭王与文祥决定托付四个人去平这三处的叛乱。第一个仍然是曾国藩。在十月初一曾国荃功成身退，率领裁撤的湘军回湖南的同时，朝中有一道廷寄递到江宁，说『江宁已臻底平，军务业经藏事，即着曾国藩酌带所部，前赴皖鄂交界，督兵剿贼，务期迅速前进，勿少延缓。』这所谓『贼』，便是捻匪。
en: As news of Ma Xinyi’s appointment reached Zhejiang, an important and intriguing report arrived from Jiangxi: the young rebel Hong Tianguifu had at last been captured. The campaign against the Taipings was drawing to a close, but formidable work remained before disorder could be put down. In the judgment of Prince Gong and Wenxiang, three rebellions still stood between the empire and lasting peace: the Taiping remnants who had fled south, the Nian bands disturbing the central provinces, and the Muslim rebellions devastating the western frontier. Fortunately, men of talent abounded in numbers surpassing earlier reigns. Prince Gong and Wenxiang decided to entrust the suppression of these three troubles to four men. The first was still Zeng Guofan. On the first day of the tenth month, as Zeng Guoquan retired in triumph and led the disbanded Hunan troops home, a confidential dispatch reached Jiangning: “Jiangning is now entirely pacified, and military operations there are concluded. Zeng Guofan shall select a portion of his forces and proceed to the Anhui–Hubei border to direct the suppression of the rebels. He must advance speedily and permit no delay.” These “rebels” were the Nian.

zh: 捻匪原以皖北为老巢，自经僧王全力攻剿，流窜到湖北、河南一带。张洛行虽死，他的侄子张总愚亦非弱者；加以陈玉成的旧部赖文光由关中回窜，因为『天京』已破，成了丧家之犬，自然而然地与捻匪合流，大为猖獗。朝廷深知僧王的马队，追奔逐北，将捻匪撵来撵去的打法，并非善策；一旦疲于奔命，为捻匪反扑，非大败不可。同时，又因为僧王的身分尊贵，连西宫太后都不能不格外优容，是位极难伺候的王爷，指授方略，则『将在外君命有所不受』；稍加督责又怕惹恼了他，索性独断独行。因此，倒不如设法让他交卸军权，回京享福，才是公私两便之计。能代僧王指挥数省的，只有一个曾国藩。不仅威望足够；而且他那『先求稳当，次求变化』，以静制静，稳扎稳打的作风，亦正可救僧王之失。至于筹饷之责，朝廷也想到了一个必不可少的人。
en: The Nian had originally made northern Anhui their base. Under Prince Sengge Rinchen’s vigorous attacks, they had moved into Hubei and Henan. Though Zhang Luoxing was dead, his nephew Zhang Zongyu was no weak successor. Lai Wenguang, formerly one of Chen Yucheng’s commanders, had also returned from Guanzhong. With the Heavenly Capital fallen, he was a man without a home; naturally he joined the Nian, greatly increasing their strength and boldness. The court knew that the prince’s cavalry tactics—pursuing and driving the Nian from place to place—were unsound. Once his troops exhausted themselves, a rebel counterattack must bring disaster. Yet his exalted position made him extremely difficult to handle. Even the Western Empress Dowager had to show him special indulgence. Offer strategic instructions, and he could invoke the maxim that a commander in the field need not obey every order of his sovereign. Press him a little, and he might take offense and act entirely on his own. It would be better, for public and private reasons alike, to find a way for him to relinquish his command and return to enjoy life in Beijing. Only Zeng Guofan could replace him in directing operations across several provinces. His prestige was sufficient, and his practice of “seeking security first and flexibility afterward”—meeting movement with stillness, advancing steadily from firm positions—would correct the prince’s mistakes. For the financing of the campaign, the court had thought of another indispensable man.

zh: 这个人就是李鸿章.上谕派他接替曾国藩，暂署两江总督；江苏巡抚则调慈禧太后的恩人，漕运总督吴棠署理。上谕中虽未明言，曾国藩带兵驻扎皖鄂交界，从路粮台由李鸿章 负其全责；可是这样部署的用意是很明白的，第一，曾、李师生，『有事弟子服其劳』，天经地义；第二，李鸿章 带兵，曾国藩替他筹过饷，如今曾国藩带兵，自然该李鸿章 筹饷；第三，两江最富，是海内最主要的一处饷源，所以谁当两江总督，都有筹饷的责任。这样的安排，就大局而言，不能算错；只是委屈了曾国藩，便宜了李鸿章与吴棠，可也就顾不得那么许多了。
en: That man was Li Hongzhang. An edict appointed him to act in Zeng’s place as Governor-General of Liangjiang, while Wu Tang, Director-General of Grain Transport and a benefactor of Empress Dowager Cixi, was transferred to act as Governor of Jiangsu. The decree did not expressly state that Li would bear full responsibility for the rear supply bureau supporting Zeng on the Anhui–Hubei frontier, but the intention was plain. First, Zeng and Li were teacher and pupil; it was only proper that “when there is work to be done, the disciple undertakes the labor.” Second, Zeng had raised funds when Li commanded in the field; now their roles should be reversed. Third, Liangjiang was the richest region and a principal source of military revenue, so whoever governed it was bound to provide funds. Viewed in terms of the general situation, the arrangement was sound. It merely disadvantaged Zeng and benefited Li and Wu—but not every consideration could be accommodated.

zh: 再有一个是杨岳斌。他是与彭玉麟齐名的水师名将，本名杨载福；因为同治皇帝这一辈，玉牒谱系上第一字为『载』，不免有犯讳的不便，所以改名岳斌。当江宁未克复以前，他已升任陕甘总督；打算赋以敉平回乱的重任。回乱不仅生于陕甘；也生于云南与新疆。云南将次平服，而新疆方兴未艾；朝廷寄望于新封子爵的鲍超，特降温旨，认为新疆平乱，『非得勇略出群如鲍超者，前往剿办，恐难壁垒一新』，所以命曾国藩传旨鲍超，在他回籍葬亲的两月假期一满，『即行由川起程，出关剿办回乱。』恭王和文祥知道鲍超好名，特地拿乾嘉名将杨遇春，与他相提并论，很灌了一番米汤。上谕中说∶『从前回疆用兵，杨遇春即系川省土著，立功边域，彪炳旅常。鲍超务当督率诸国，肃清西陲，威扬万里，以与前贤后先辉映。该提督忠勇性成，接奉此旨，必即遵行，以逼朝廷委任。』话说得很诚挚，而命曾国藩传旨，亦有暗示他帮着催劝之意。无奈曾国藩对湘军的急流勇退，明哲保身，早有定算；鲍超是他的爱将，当然要加意保全，所以只是照例传旨，并不劝驾。
en: Another man selected was Yang Yuebin, a naval commander whose fame equaled Peng Yulin’s. His original name was Yang Zaifu. Since the first character of the Tongzhi Emperor’s generation in the imperial genealogy was Zai, however, the name risked offending the naming taboo, and he changed it to Yuebin. Before Jiangning fell he had already been appointed Governor-General of Shaanxi and Gansu, with the intention of entrusting him with the suppression of the Muslim rebellion. Such rebellions had broken out not only there but in Yunnan and Xinjiang as well. Yunnan was approaching pacification, while Xinjiang’s troubles were gathering force. For the latter, the court placed its hopes in the newly created viscount Bao Chao. A warmly worded decree declared that without “a man of exceptional courage and strategy such as Bao Chao” it would be difficult to transform the military situation in Xinjiang. Zeng was therefore ordered to transmit instructions that, upon the expiry of Bao’s two-month leave to bury his parent, he should “depart immediately from Sichuan, pass beyond the frontier, and suppress the Muslim rebellion.” Knowing Bao’s love of renown, Prince Gong and Wenxiang flattered him by comparing him with Yang Yuchun, the celebrated general of the Qianlong and Jiaqing reigns. “In former campaigns in the Muslim territories, Yang Yuchun, himself a native of Sichuan, won frontier victories whose glory shone upon the military banners. Bao Chao must lead his forces to pacify the western marches, carrying his fame ten thousand li and matching the splendor of his predecessor. Loyal and brave by nature, he will surely obey upon receiving this decree and fulfill the court’s trust.” The language was most earnest. By requiring Zeng to transmit it, the court also hinted that he should help urge Bao forward. Zeng, however, had long resolved that the Hunan Army should withdraw prudently at the height of its success. Bao was a favorite commander whom he particularly wished to protect. He simply conveyed the edict in the usual way and offered no encouragement to depart.

zh: 再有一个朝廷寄以重望的，便是左宗棠。他是现任的闽浙总督，由江西瑞金为鲍超所败，而窜入福建境内的李世贤、汪海洋两大股，顺理成章 地该由他负责清剿。左宗棠不是怕事的人，对此亦自觉当仁不让，义不容辞；可是朝廷一连串的处置，却使他即气又急，愤愤不平。首先大失所望的是，浙江巡抚派了马新贻；蒋益澧落了空，也就等于是他失去了浙江这个地盘。其次是李鸿章 调署两江，名位已在己之上，使他很不舒服。其次是在江西的陕甘总督杨岳斌，奉旨迅即到任；朝廷责成浙江每月拨给陕甘协饷十万两，并先筹措八万银子，作为杨军的开拔费用。为此，左宗棠的肝火很旺，每日接见僚属，大骂曾国藩、李鸿章 和郭嵩焘。这样骂了几天，怒火稍减；想想既不肯辞官归田，就得有声有色地大干一番。军务是有把握的，就是饷源越来越绌，得要找个足智多谋的人，趁马新贻末曾到任以前，好好筹划妥当。
en: The other man in whom the court placed great hopes was Zuo. As Governor-General of Fujian and Zhejiang, he was naturally responsible for suppressing the two large forces of Li Shixian and Wang Haiyang, defeated by Bao at Ruijin in Jiangxi and driven into Fujian. Zuo was not a man to shrink from trouble. He regarded the duty as his by right and could not honorably refuse. Yet a succession of court decisions made him angry, anxious, and deeply resentful. His first disappointment was Ma Xinyi’s appointment to Zhejiang. Jiang Yili had been passed over, which meant that Zuo had lost control of the province. Next came Li’s transfer to act as Governor-General of Liangjiang, placing him above Zuo in standing and precedence—a most unpleasant thought. Then Yang Yuebin, still in Jiangxi, was ordered to proceed promptly to his post in Shaanxi and Gansu. Zhejiang was required to contribute a hundred thousand taels a month toward his military expenses and first to raise eighty thousand for his army’s departure. Zuo’s temper flared. Every day, when receiving his staff, he roundly abused Zeng Guofan, Li Hongzhang, and Guo Songtao. After several days his anger abated a little. Since he would not resign and return to farming, he must undertake something substantial and impressive. He was confident of his military ability; the difficulty was an ever-shrinking revenue base. Before Ma arrived, he needed a resourceful man to help arrange matters properly.

zh: 这个人自然非胡雪岩莫属。『雪翁，』他说，『你看，挤得我无路可走了！你算算看，我该到哪里筹饷？哪里都难！』两个人将十五行省一个一个地算。除开穷瘠的省份，有饷可筹的富庶之地，都已为他人早着先鞭；江苏、安徽是两江辖区，曾李师弟的势力，根深蒂固；江西沈葆桢，对待曾军的前例，足以令人望而却步；山东、山西供应京饷，而且两省巡抚阎敬铭、沈桂芬清刚精明，都不是好相与的人；湖北食用川盐，在沙市设局征厘，收入相当可观，可是官文是督抚中唯一的一个旗人，有理无理，皆受朝廷袒护，不容易打得进去；至于天府之国的四川，有骆秉章 在那里，顾念旧日宾主之谊，自然不好意思唱一出『取成都』。『福建穷得很；我能筹饷的地方，只有贵省和广东了。东该给我的饷不给；可恨郭筠仙，心目中只认得曾涤生、李少荃。此恨难消！』左宗棠停了一下又说，『至于马谷山，听说倒还讲理；不过既是曾涤生所保，又是李少荃的同年，不见得肯助我一臂。雪翁，你看我该怎么办？』
en: That man could only be Hu. “Mr Xueyan,” Zuo said, “they have squeezed me until I have nowhere to turn. Where do you think I can raise funds? It is difficult everywhere.” Together they went through the fifteen provinces one by one. Leaving aside the poor provinces, every wealthy source of revenue had already been claimed. Jiangsu and Anhui lay within Liangjiang, where Zeng and his pupil Li were deeply entrenched. Shen Baozhen’s treatment of the Hunan Army in Jiangxi was warning enough. Shandong and Shanxi supplied the capital, and their governors, Yan Jingming and Shen Guifen, were upright, shrewd, and difficult men to deal with. Hubei consumed Sichuan salt, collecting substantial likin revenue through an office at Shashi. But Guanwen was the only bannerman among the governors and governors-general; right or wrong, he enjoyed the court’s protection, and gaining access there would be hard. As for prosperous Sichuan, Luo Bingzhang governed it. Remembering their old relationship as patron and secretary, Zuo could hardly bring himself to play out a “seizure of Chengdu.” “Fujian is desperately poor. The only places left to me are your province and Guangdong. Guangdong withholds the contributions due to me. That hateful Guo Yunxian recognizes no one but Zeng Disheng and Li Shaoquan! I cannot forget it.” Zuo paused. “As for Ma Gushan, I hear he is reasonable enough. But Zeng recommended him, and he passed the examinations in the same year as Li. He may not be willing to help me. Mr Xueyan, what am I to do?”

zh: 胡雪岩默然。因为他觉得自己的处境很难，左宗棠的知遇要报答；而浙江是自己的家乡，为左宗棠设谋画策，可不能挨地方父老的骂。胡雪岩一向言词爽利，而且不管天大的难事，一诺无辞；象这样迟疑不答的情形，可说绝无仅有。左宗棠微感诧异，不免追问缘故。『不瞒大人说，我很为难。大人现在只有浙江一个地盘，粮饷当然出在浙江，筹得少了不够用；筹得多了，苦了地方。说起来是我胡某人出的主意；本乡本土，我不大好做人。』雪岩又说，『如果大人兼署浙江巡抚，我还可以出出主意，截长补短，见机行事，总还兼顾得到。现在换了马中丞，我又是分发江西的试用道，是大人奏调我在浙江当差；大人一离浙江，我当然不能再问浙江的公事，善后局的差使亦要交卸，何况其他？』
en: Hu remained silent. His position was difficult. He must repay Zuo’s recognition and favor, yet Zhejiang was his home province. He could not devise schemes for Zuo that would earn the curses of its people. Hu usually spoke decisively and accepted even the greatest difficulties without hesitation; such a prolonged silence was almost unprecedented. Mildly surprised, Zuo pressed him for an explanation. “To be frank, my lord, I am in a difficult position. Zhejiang is now the only province you can draw upon, so naturally your supplies and pay must come from it. Raise too little, and it will not suffice; raise too much, and the people suffer. Everyone will say it was my idea. Among my own countrymen, that would be an uncomfortable position. If you continued to act as Governor of Zhejiang, I could still suggest ways to balance one source against another and adapt to circumstances, taking both interests into account. But Governor Ma is coming. I am only a probationary circuit intendant assigned to Jiangxi, whom you had transferred here for service. Once you leave Zhejiang, I shall have no right to concern myself with its affairs. I must even hand over my post at the Reconstruction Bureau, let alone anything else.”

zh: 他一路说，左宗棠一路点头，等他说完，做个『稍安毋躁』的手势答道∶『你刚才所说的情形，我完全清楚，我们要好好谈谈。万变不离的宗旨是∶雪翁，你仍旧要帮我的忙。怎么个帮法，我们回头再商量，现在先谈你的难处；诚如所言，我现在只有浙江一个地盘，粮饷只有着落在浙江，而且要定一个确数，按月一定汇到，连日子都错不得一天。雪翁，凡事先讲理，后讲情；情理都站得住，还争不过人家，我当然也有我的手段。』胡雪岩不知他最后这几句话，意何所指？只能就事论事，问一事∶『大人预备定一个啥数目？』『你看呢？』左宗棠放低了声音说∶『我们自己人，我告诉你实话∶我的兵，实数一万八千，不过筹饷要宽，照两万三千人算。』胡雪岩的心算极快。士兵每人每月饷银、军粮、器械、弹药、马草，加上营帐、锅碗等等杂支，平均要五两银子；两万三千人就是十一万五千两。另加统帅个人的用途；文案、委员的薪水伙食；送往迎来的应酬费用，每个月非十五万银子不可。
en: Zuo nodded throughout. When Hu finished, he gestured for patience. “I understand all the circumstances you have described. We must discuss them carefully. Through every change, one principle remains: you must continue to help me. How you are to help we shall consider presently. First, let us deal with your difficulty. As you say, Zhejiang is my only base, and Zhejiang must provide my army’s funds. Moreover, there must be a fixed sum, remitted each month on a fixed date, not one day late. Mr Xueyan, in everything we first establish what is reasonable, then appeal to personal feeling. If both reason and feeling support us and we still cannot prevail, I naturally have methods of my own.” Hu did not know what the last words implied. Keeping to the immediate issue, he asked, “What sum do you intend to fix, my lord?” “What would you suggest?” Zuo lowered his voice. “Between ourselves, I shall tell you the truth. I actually have eighteen thousand men, but funding must allow a margin. We should calculate for twenty-three thousand.” Hu reckoned rapidly. A soldier’s monthly pay, grain, weapons, ammunition, horse fodder, and miscellaneous needs—tents, cooking pots, bowls, and the rest—averaged five taels. Twenty-three thousand men meant a hundred and fifteen thousand taels. Add the commander’s own expenses, the salaries and board of secretaries and commissioned officials, and the costs of hospitality, and no less than a hundred and fifty thousand taels a month would do.

zh: 这笔巨数，由浙江独力负担，未免太重；胡雪岩便很婉转地说道∶『闽浙一家。福建拨给浙江的协饷，前后总计，不下三百万两之多；如今福建有事，当然要帮忙。而况大人带的又是浙江的兵，理当浙江支饷。不过，浙江的情形，大人是再明白不过的；如果能够量出为入，事情就好办了。』成语是量入为出，胡雪岩却反过来说，倒也新鲜；左宗棠便捻着八字胡子，含笑问道∶『何以谓之量出为入？倒要请教。』『譬如一碗汤，你也舀，他也舀，到嘴都有限┅┅。』『啊！』左宗棠抢着说道∶『我懂了！我亦本有此意，第一，陕甘的协饷，决不能答应；第二，广东解浙江的协饷，有名无实，我要奏请停拨。』说到这里，他眼珠打转，慢慢地笑了，笑得极其诡秘。
en: For Zhejiang to bear that enormous sum alone was too much. Hu therefore spoke tactfully. “Fujian and Zhejiang are one family. Over the years, Fujian has contributed at least three million taels toward Zhejiang’s military expenses. Now that Fujian has trouble, we should naturally help. Besides, the troops you command are Zhejiang troops; Zhejiang ought to pay them. But you understand the province’s condition better than anyone. If we could determine our income by our expenditure, matters would be easier.” The usual maxim was to determine expenditure by income; Hu had reversed it, which was something new. Stroking his drooping mustache, Zuo asked with a smile, “What do you mean by determining income by expenditure? I should like to hear.” “Suppose there is a bowl of soup. One man takes a ladleful, another takes a ladleful; very little reaches anyone’s mouth—” “Ah!” Zuo interrupted. “I understand. I had the same thought. First, we absolutely cannot agree to the contribution for Shaanxi and Gansu. Second, Guangdong’s contribution to Zhejiang exists only in name. I shall petition to have it discontinued.” At this his eyes moved from side to side, and a slow, exceedingly secretive smile spread over his face.

zh: 这一笑，大有文章.胡雪岩觉得非搞明白不可；便有意套问一句∶『广东的协饷是个画饼，虽不能充饥，看看也是好的。』『不然！奏请停拨，就是要让朝廷知道，这是个画饼。雪翁，』左宗棠突然兴奋了，『你看老夫的手段！画饼要把它变成个又大又厚，足供一饱的大麦饼。你信不信？』『怎么不信？』胡雪岩紧接着问，『大人变这套戏法，可要我做下手？』『当然！少了你，我这套平地抠饼，外带大锯活人的戏法就变不成了。』『大锯活人』四字，虽是戏言，却也刺耳，胡雪岩便用半开玩笑的语气问道∶『大人，你要锯哪一个？』『哪一个？』左宗棠有种狞笑的神色，『锯我那位亲家。』胡雪岩骇然。他早知左宗棠跟郭嵩焘有心病，而此心病，不但未能由时光来冲淡，反有与日俱深之势；但何致于说出『大锯活人』的这样的话来？因此一时楞在那里作声不得。左宗棠的脸上，也收起嬉笑之态，变得相当认真，眼睁得好在，嘴闭得好紧；但眼神闪烁，嘴唇翕动，竟似心湖中起了极大的波澜似的。这就使得胡雪岩越发贯注全神，要听他如何『大锯活人』了。
en: There was much behind that smile. Hu felt he must understand it and deliberately probed. “Guangdong’s contribution is a picture of a cake. Though it cannot feed us, it is something to look at.” “No. By asking for its cancellation, I shall show the court that it is only a painted cake. Mr Xueyan—” Zuo suddenly grew excited. “Watch this old man’s methods! I shall turn the painted cake into a great thick barley cake, enough to fill our bellies. Do you believe me?” “Of course. Will you need me as an assistant in this conjuring trick?” “Naturally! Without you I could never perform this trick of producing a cake from bare ground—and sawing a living man in two besides.” Though meant as a joke, the last words were jarring. Half in jest, Hu asked, “Whom do you mean to saw in two, my lord?” “Whom?” Zuo’s smile had grown fierce. “My own in-law.” Hu was appalled. He had long known that Zuo bore a grievance against Guo Songtao, one that time had deepened rather than eased. But how had it reached the point of such language? For a moment he stood speechless. Zuo too ceased smiling. His face grew serious, his eyes wide, his mouth firmly closed; yet his gaze flickered and his lips moved, as though powerful waves were passing through his mind. Hu listened with even closer attention to hear how this “sawing a living man in two” was to be done.

zh: 『雪岩！』左宗棠第一次改口，以别字相呼，表示对胡雪岩以密友看待，『你的书读得不多，我是知道的；不过「世事洞明皆学问」，照这一层来说，我佩服你。』『不敢当。』胡雪岩有些局促，但也很率直，『大人有什么话要说，尽管吩咐；拿顶「高帽子」套在我头上，就有点吃不消了。』『你我之间，何用要什么送高帽子的手段？我的意思是，我的为人，我的处世，只有你能明白五分；还有五分，你不但不明白，或许还会大不以为然。这就因为你少读书；如果你也多读过一点书，就会明白我那另外五分，而且谅解我不得不然；势所必然！』原来如此，胡雪岩倒有些受宠若惊了，『大人』他说∶『你老跟我谈「大家之道，在明明德」，我是不懂的。』『我不跟你谈经，我跟你谈史。雪岩，我先请问你两句成语，「大义灭亲」、「公而忘私」怎么讲？』
en: “Xueyan!” For the first time Zuo dropped the formal address and used his courtesy name, treating him as an intimate friend. “I know you have not read many books. But understanding the world is itself learning, and in that respect I admire you.” “You are too kind.” Hu was a little uneasy but remained frank. “If you have something to say, please give me your instructions. Such a tall hat of praise is rather too much for me.” “Why should I need flattery between us? What I mean is that you understand half of my character and conduct. The other half you not only fail to understand, but may strongly disapprove of. That is because you have read too little. If you had studied more, you would understand that other half as well, and see that I have no choice: circumstances compel it.” So that was what he meant. Hu felt almost overwhelmed by the confidence shown him. “My lord, if you speak to me of ‘the Way of Great Learning lies in manifesting luminous virtue,’ I shall understand nothing.” “I shall speak of history, not the Classics. First, tell me what these two sayings mean: ‘For a greater righteousness, sacrifice even one’s kin,’ and ‘For public duty, forget private interests.’”

zh: 胡雪岩无以为答；觉得也不必答，老实回复∶『大人不要考我了。就从这两句成语上头，谈你老的打算。』『我不是考你，我的意思是，我的行事，照世俗之见，或许会大大地骂我。不过，我的行事，于亲有亏，于义无悖；于私有惭，于公无愧。这都非世俗之见所能谅解，而只有读过书的人，才会在心里说一声∶左某人命世之英，不得不然。』这段话很掉了几句文，不过胡雪岩也大致还能听得懂；而且听出意思，他对郭嵩焘要下辣手了！所想不通的是，他有何辣手可对郭嵩焘？他的疑问，立刻得到了解答；左宗棠起身坐在书桌前面，伸毫铺纸，很快地画成一幅地图，在那些曲线、圆点之中，写上地名；胡雪岩看出是一幅闽粤交界的形势图。『李世贤在漳州。漳州是九月十四沦陷的，总兵禄魁阵亡；汀漳龙道徐晓峰殉难。李世贤大概有八千多人，不可轻敌。』左宗棠又指着长汀、连城、上杭这三角地带说∶『汪海洋在这一带；照我的看法，他比李世贤更凶悍。然而，不足为虑，贼不足平！雪岩，你这几年总也懂得一点兵法了！你看李、汪二贼的出路在哪里？』
en: Hu had no answer, nor felt one was needed. He replied honestly, “Please do not examine me, my lord. Begin with those sayings and tell me your plans.” “I am not examining you. My point is that ordinary people may condemn my actions bitterly. Yet though I fail my kin, I do not fail what is right; though I may be ashamed in private relationships, I have nothing to blush for in public duty. Common opinion cannot understand this. Only a learned man will say in his heart: ‘Zuo is a hero born for his age. He could do no otherwise.’” The speech was rather bookish, but Hu understood it well enough and grasped its implication: Zuo meant to deal Guo Songtao a severe blow. What he could not see was what blow lay within Zuo’s power. His question was answered at once. Zuo rose, sat at his desk, took a brush, and spread out paper. He rapidly drew a map, adding place-names among the curved lines and dots. Hu recognized the Fujian–Guangdong frontier. “Li Shixian is at Zhangzhou, which fell on the fourteenth day of the ninth month. Brigade Commander Lukui was killed in action; Circuit Intendant Xu Xiaofeng of Tingzhou, Zhangzhou, and Longyan died at his post. Li has probably more than eight thousand men and must not be underestimated.” Pointing to the triangle formed by Changting, Liancheng, and Shanghang, Zuo continued, “Wang Haiyang is here. In my judgment he is fiercer than Li. Still, there is no cause for alarm about putting these rebels down. Xueyan, you must have learned a little strategy in recent years. Where do you think Li and Wang can escape?”

zh: 这一下好象考倒了胡雪岩。他仔细看了半天，方始答说『他们是由西面江西逃过来的；往东是出海，有好长一段路，再说没有船也出不了海。北面呢，大人带兵压了下来，啊，』胡雪岩恍然大悟，很有把握地说∶『这两个长毛的出路，只有南面的广东，嘉应州首当其冲！』左宗棠深深点头，拈髭微笑，『对，』他说，『嘉应州首当其冲！到了那时候充饥的就不是画饼了！』语中有深意。左宗棠没有说下去；胡雪岩不便回——怕自己猜错了，冒昧一关，是大大的失言。谁知左宗棠毫不忌讳，真的拿胡雪岩当可共极端机密的心腹看待，『郭筠仙一直担心曾涤生「驱寇入粤」，他没有想到「驱寇入粤」的是他的亲家。』他说∶『雪岩，到那时候，又另是一番局面了。』胡雪岩不自觉地打了个寒噤，觉得左宗棠的手段真是太辣了些！虽然，这正是他所猜想到的，但测度是测度，听别人亲口证实，感觉又自不同。
en: For a moment Hu seemed stumped. He studied the map closely before answering. “They came from Jiangxi in the west. To the east lies the sea, a long way off—and without ships they could not put to sea anyway. In the north, your troops are pressing down. Ah!” Understanding came suddenly, and he spoke with confidence. “Their only way out is south into Guangdong. Jiaying Prefecture will bear the first attack.” Zuo nodded deeply, stroking his mustache with a smile. “Exactly. Jiaying will bear the first attack. Then we shall no longer be feeding ourselves on painted cakes.” There was a hidden meaning in his words. He did not continue, and Hu dared not ask, fearing that a mistaken guess might lead him into a grave indiscretion. Zuo, however, had no such reservations. He truly regarded Hu as a confidant fit to hear the deepest secrets. “Guo Yunxian has always feared that Zeng Disheng would drive the rebels into Guangdong. He never imagined it would be his own in-law who did so. When that happens, Xueyan, the situation will be entirely different.” Hu shuddered involuntarily. Zuo’s methods seemed altogether too ruthless. He had guessed this very thing, certainly; but a conjecture was one matter, and hearing it confirmed in the man’s own words was another.

zh: 『雪岩，』左宗棠问道∶『你倒说说看到那时候是怎么样的一番局面？』『是。』胡雪岩想了想说，『到那时候，朝廷当然借重大人的威望，拜钦差大臣，节制福建、浙江、广东三省的军务。郭中丞——。』他没有再说下去；意思是郭嵩焘在左宗棠『大锯活人』的摆布之下，非吃足苦头不可。『不错，此亦是势所必然之事。到那时候，雪岩，我不会再累浙江了，不怕郭筠仙不乖乖替我筹饷。不过，』左宗棠沉吟了好一会，『也说不定！郭筠仙愚而好自用；怕他仍旧执迷不悟。』『果然如此，大人又怎么办？』
en: “Xueyan, tell me what the situation will be then.” “Yes.” Hu considered. “The court will naturally turn to your prestige and ability, appoint you imperial commissioner, and place military affairs in Fujian, Zhejiang, and Guangdong under your authority. Governor Guo—” He stopped. His meaning was clear: under Zuo’s handling, Guo would suffer severely. “Precisely. Circumstances must lead to that. Then, Xueyan, I shall no longer burden Zhejiang. Guo Yunxian will have to raise funds obediently for me. Unless—” Zuo pondered for a long while. “There is no certainty. Guo is foolish and obstinate. He may still refuse to see reason.” “And if he does, my lord, what will you do?”
